newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Electronics 58 pct of Singapore domestic exports.
newsitem.headline: Electronics 58 pct of Singapore domestic exports.

text.p: Electronics and related products accounted for 58 percent of Singapore's total domestic exports in 1996, the Trade Development Board (TDB) said on Sunday.
Electronics made up only 28 percent of Singapore's domestic exports in 1986, the TDB said in a statement.
It said Singapore's domestic exports of chemical products had also experienced strong growth of 12.2 percent per annum over the last decade.
The TDB attributed the growth in non-oil domestic exports, particularly electronics, to rapid industrialisation and increased foreign investment in the Asia-Pacific region.
The United States, ASEAN, the European Union, Japan and Hong Kong absorbed 82 percent of Singapore's non-oil domestic exports in 1996, against 79.5 percent in 1986.
Re-exports of machinery and transport equipment made up 63 percent of total re-exports in 1996, up from 37 percent in 1986.
Japan and the ASEAN countries had remained Singapore's top sources of imports over the last decade, the TDB said.
It said Singapore was ranked the second most competitive business location after the United States/Canada in a survey of 280 Singapore-based companies.
